verification_report.summary: The proof was checked sequentially and establishes both target (I) and the conditional criterion (4.1), including all three stated sufficient cases. The fixed-neighborhood approximation and decreasing-subsequence argument correctly place A in the locally approachable class without identifying A with all of CPsh. The required positivity, coefficient-measure calculus, analytic-nullity theorem, and canonical multiplicity formula match their stated uses in [CLD, arXiv:1204.6277v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2). The actual analytic components are locally finite, and their crossings are closed analytic subsets of smaller dimension, as supplied by [Ducros, Section 4](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2470.pdf). For (I), canonical equality confines each component difference to its crossing locus; separate total-variation nullity of both positive curvature coefficients then forces that difference to vanish. For (4.1), positivity of component curvatures holds for the full minimal uniform-closure sheaf, and the positive multiplicity decomposition gives measure domination by the common curvature. The assumed crossing-nullity therefore yields the same vanishing argument. An approachable given potential, a local approachable potential for the common curvature, and zero common curvature each supply the required hypothesis. Nonreduced multiplicities are retained, compact-local arguments avoid global paracompactness, and no usual-strictness inheritance by arbitrary ordinary opens is needed. No classification or unrestricted CPsh analytic-nullity assertion is used. The required theorem-search calls were attempted; their endpoint was unavailable, so all references were verified using the web fallback and direct primary-source inspection. No critical errors or gaps were found.
